top_choice_rationale: Base editing (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) is a designed, mechanistically explicit chemical transformation of a single nucleotide; the adenine editor needed directed evolution of TadA to act on DNA, a reaction no natural enzyme performs. It is reproduced widely, already has clinical use, and splits cleanly into two attributable founding inventions. Residual risks are proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize and Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID, which citation wording can address. Targeted protein degradation is a coherent second choice but lacks an approved degrader and has a harder attribution cut; phase separation is contested in vivo; nitrogenase is structure-only with the mechanism unresolved.
